I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. I ran the same script on Q2 first, and it reproduced all ten of your reference values exactly.

| | Q3 2025 |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net revenue | consumer, 330,713,158 KRW |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 249 |
| c. Category with the highest net revenue | hw, 294,122,476 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net revenue | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u141@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 232 |
| g. Average net revenue per order | 714,970 KRW |
| h. September vs. August growth | -2.6% |

The data needed three adjustments before the Q2 values matched:
- **Timezone:** order times are stored in UTC. Your Q2 values only came out when I converted them to Korea time (UTC+9) to set the quarter and month boundaries. Using UTC as-is gave different values.
- **Messy labels:** some segment names differ only in capitals or extra spaces (e.g. `SMB` and `smb`, `" consumer"`). I trimmed spaces and lowercased them so each counts as one segment. I did the same for category, status and email.
- **Duplicate customers:** the customer table has 300 rows but only 250 distinct emails. For b, e and f, I counted each email as one customer.

STATUS: DONE
